purpose: Per-L1-class specialists for rare L2 subcategory classification
status: EVALUATED — all three excluded from final hybrid system

training.approach: One model per L1 class with rare subcategories (< T_rare samples)

evaluation.problem: Poorly calibrated — predict_proba returns high confidence even on wrong predictions; not comparable to CamemBERT softmax

training.approach: One LoRA adapter per L1 class with rare subcategories

evaluation.problem: L1 classifier has ~8% error rate; on hard samples (where specialists are needed) error rate is much higher → wrong L1 → wrong adapter → catastrophic

generative.approach: Constrained log-probability scoring over valid L2 candidates
generative.description: For each product, compute P(label | prompt) for every valid subcategory within the predicted L1 class. Pick the label with highest log-prob.

evaluation.problem: Consistently underperforms CamemBERT even on ambiguous/low-confidence samples

why_specialists_fail: L1 routing is the bottleneck: 8% error on average, much higher on hard samples
Wrong L1 prediction → wrong specialist → accuracy drops to 1-5%
SetFit confidence is not calibrated — cannot be compared to CamemBERT softmax
Generative models lack the discriminative precision needed for 6K-class taxonomy
Only XGBoost (in Gated+Hybrid/) succeeds because it's well-calibrated and batch-efficient
key_findings.recommendation: Use CamemBERT L2 + XGBoost max_conf hybrid instead (see Gated+Hybrid/)

dataset.note: Specialists trained only on subcategories with < T_rare training samples per L1 class
